text:
Viktor Arvidsson is on his fifth NHL team, and at 33 he's playing like Detroit was the right call. The Detroit News called him a "productive free-agent signing" last week, and the numbers back the headline.

Eight goals in 17 games, seven of his 15 points on the power play, and a hat trick against Chicago on Oct. 29. None of it is smoke. His 8.96 expected goals (the quality of his chances) say the goals are earned, and he's actually scored about one fewer than those chances suggest. His 1.68 expected goals per 60 is up from 1.35 last season in Boston, where he scored 25.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains the style: 99th percentile for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net last season. He doesn't need speed (EDGE has him in the 24th percentile for top speed); he needs to arrive at the right spot, and he does.

He's pointless in his last two games, both losses, with five shots between them. Our range has him at 29 to 46 goals. If we're wrong about anything, it's that the low end is too cautious.
headline: Arvidsson's move to Detroit is working
